QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_6

question.text: Ms. Kavita Rao, a family office CIO, briefs Mr. Suresh Patel (Manager of Kaveri Private Credit AIF - Category II): 'Our patriarch wants medium-to-long horizon exposure to later-stage unlisted companies whose business plans have already been validated by institutional investors; he has deep pockets and high illiquidity tolerance, and is agnostic to debt or equity.' Which AIF product set BEST matches this investor profile per the Chapter 3 suitability illustrations?

answer.text: Category I Angel Funds and early-stage VC funds, because the family office has high risk appetite
Category II Private Equity Funds (for validated later-stage companies) and Category II Private Debt Funds, including venture debt, for the debt/equity-agnostic exposure
Category III Hedge Funds using long-short and market-neutral strategies
Listed-market PMS with a concentrated small-cap mandate

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the Chapter 3 suitability table and illustrations, family offices and other long-term pools map to Category II PE for validated later-stage companies and to Category II debt/private credit (including venture debt) where the investor is debt/equity agnostic. The patriarch's profile — medium-to-long horizon, validated later-stage unlisted exposure, deep pockets, high illiquidity tolerance and indifference between debt and equity — matches this Category II PE-plus-private-credit combination. The Trap: Option A (Angel Funds and early-stage VC) targets a smaller-ticket, higher-risk early-stage profile and does not fit a 'validated business plans' brief. Option C is Category III hedge-fund territory and is outside Category I/II suitability for this profile. Option D is listed-securities PMS and is not an AIF product set. Note: Be careful with Special Situations Funds — the workbook classifies SSFs as Category I, not Category II, so a 'best fit' Category II product set for this investor centres on PE for validated companies and private credit/venture debt.
